answer: Work is measured in elapsed time, not watts. Each seat receives a verifiable delay function whose length grows with the index it is granted, and only a fully sequential run of that function unlocks its payout, so the k-th seat costs more wall-clock time than every earlier one combined. A clone farm cannot parallelize it: each thread is inherently serial and a finished proof cannot be copied onto a second seat. The honest newcomer pays one short voyage; an operator of many pays a sum that climbs faster than the count, and the echo of a single saved proof opens no second door.
